headline: OKO HITS 1KM: G2 Goldfields Drills 84.5m @ 3.0 g/t Au Amid GMIN's C$3B Takeover
snippet: G2 Goldfields pushed the OKO project in Guyana to 1km depth with hole GDD277B returning 84.5m at 3.0 g/t Au from 915m depth, including 6.0m at 13.4 g/t Au — the deepest intercept at OKO to date, extending mineralization 140m vertically where it remains open. Results arrive weeks before G Mining Ventures is expected to close its C$3B acquisition of G2.

headline: ALASKA GOLD BREAKTHROUGH: Freegold Ventures Drills 74.9m @ 1.43 g/t Au at Golden Summit
snippet: Freegold Ventures reported today a 74.9-metre intercept grading 1.43 g/t Au at the Golden Summit project near Fairbanks, Alaska, extending continuity across the Dolphin–Cleary–WOW corridor. The result is part of an aggressive 50,000m 2026 drill program aimed at advancing toward a Preliminary Feasibility Study.

headline: GOLD $4,583 / SILVER $74.52: Metals Push Higher as Dollar Slides After Central Banks Hold Rates
snippet: Gold climbed 1.18% to $4,582.84/oz and silver gained 1.90% to $74.52/oz Tuesday as the U.S. dollar softened following coordinated rate holds by the Fed, ECB, Bank of England, and Bank of Japan. The gold-to-silver ratio held near 61.5 — silver outpacing gold for the third consecutive session, a signal that risk appetite for physical metals is broadening beyond gold.

headline: BONANZA GRADE: KLDC Hits 39.35 g/t Au Over 16.4m at Mirado Step-Out, Ontario
snippet: Kirkland Lake Discoveries (TSX-V: KLDC) hit 39.35 g/t Au over 16.4m within 50.3m of continuous mineralization at a 40m step-out at Mirado, Ontario — including a 1,670 g/t Au smear over 0.38m. Six more holes are pending assay, and management says the South Zone is far more laterally continuous than the historical interpretation suggested.

headline: COPPER MONSTER: Power Metallic Hits 17.45m @ 9.47% CuEq at Quebec's Lion Zone, MRE Next
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSX-V: PNPN) released winter 2026 assays from the Lion Zone at Nisk, Quebec: 17.45m at 9.47% CuEq including 6.30m at 17.91% CuEq, and a second hole 100m east returning 39.0m at 5.66% CuEq. Both intervals will anchor the upcoming Mineral Resource Estimate for the polymetallic project's potential open-pit starter.

headline: COPPER $5.94/LB: Iran Conflict Chokes Sulphur Supply Chain, Threatening Chilean Refining Capacity
snippet: Copper rose 2.44% to $5.94/lb ($13,095/t) Tuesday as US–Iran tensions threatened sulphur exports to China — a critical feedstock for roughly half of Chile's copper refining capacity. Combined with force majeure at Indonesia's Grasberg and guidance downgrades at Quebrada Blanca, the structural deficit story is compounding on multiple fronts simultaneously.

headline: BRAZIL'S GOLD BOOM: Junior Explorers Gain Ground as High Prices Unlock New Terrain
snippet: Permitting reforms and record-high gold prices are drawing junior exploration capital into Brazil's underexplored greenstone belts, with new programs emerging across Pará and Mato Grosso states. Analysts are drawing comparisons to the early-stage dynamics of West Africa's gold cycle from the early 2000s.

headline: SIX STRAIGHT YEARS: Silver Deficit Widens 15% in 2026, 762 Million Oz Drained from Global Stocks
snippet: The silver market posted its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2026, with the shortfall widening 15% to 46.3 million troy ounces. Cumulative drawdowns since 2021 total 762 million ounces — close to a full year of global mine production — raising urgent questions about how long remaining above-ground inventory can cover the structural gap.

headline: WHO'S WINNING the 2026 Exploration Race? Africa's Junior Mining Sector Has Answers
snippet: African Mining Online's new analysis argues the real winners of 2026's exploration cycle are companies with tight capital structures, high-grade targets, and proximity to existing infrastructure — not simply the largest drill budgets. The piece surveys who is separating from the pack across Africa's major mining belts as generalist funds return to the sector.

headline: CHINA DROPS PENALTY HAMMER on Rare Earth Producers: Fines Up to 10x Illegal Gains, Licences Revoked
snippet: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published a four-tier enforcement framework for rare earth producers: quota breaches under 10% trigger fines of up to five times illegal gains; breaches over 30% mean equipment seizure and licence revocation. A new national traceability platform will log every tonne mined, processed, and sold — tightening Beijing's grip on a supply chain it already dominates.

headline: LITHIUM RESTART NOW: Core Lithium Begins Ore Extraction at Finniss This Month After $205M Fundraise
snippet: Core Lithium's Finniss mine in Australia's Northern Territory has entered the ore extraction phase this month after securing $205 million in financing anchored by a $70 million Glencore convertible note. The restart targets 134,000 tonnes of spodumene concentrate from the Grants open pit, with first shipment aimed for Q4 2026 and a 20-year mine life projected.

headline: NEW US URANIUM MINE ONLINE: Ur-Energy Starts In-Situ Recovery Mining at Shirley Basin, Wyoming
snippet: Ur-Energy (NYSE American: URG) announced the start of uranium mining operations at its Shirley Basin ISR project in Wyoming — the company's second operating mine and one of the first new U.S. uranium operations to come online in years. The project adds to domestic supply as utilities accelerate long-term contracting to reduce dependence on foreign uranium sources.
